decisive_moments.reason: Pro directly incorporated the strongest access and novice objections by specifying hints, definitions, worked steps, and adaptive exceptions while preserving questioning as the default.

Con effectively identified risks of friction, assessment-loop behavior, and subject-specific inefficiency, but these objections mainly supported adaptation rather than disproving a question-first norm.
Pro clearly framed the policy as a defeasible default rather than an absolute rule and connected questioning to durable understanding, independence, and teacher-relevant misconception evidence.
